than ever before, yet with the readiness to resign and sacrifice
ourselves. It is such a spirit which shows that we have truly
experienced "that day"
", which proves that we are really
those who no more belong to this world. The spirit of readiness
for renunciation and sacrifice! Will it not always be painful
to see that which we had considered as our task in life
threatened, suppressed, ruined? Will it not always be deeply
painful to be wrenched from those with whom we are bound
with the ties of love? Were these things not painful, they
would not present a true sacrifice.
It might no doubt seem enticing to seek a position in life,
the opportunity of which is provided by the Roman Catholic
Church in its monastic system. There, man from the outset
and once for all severs the connexions which bind him to the
life of the world, so that nothing more can inwardly affect or
wound him. Let us moreover be on our guard against too
easily despising such an institution; for us Protestants it may
always serve as a warning sign that we too as Christians are
required to sever ourselves in spirit from the world, and to
stand before God in naked solitariness. But we feel bound to
add that this requirement is not truly fulfilled in monasti-
cism. In monasticism ultimate freedom through self-
surrender to God is not attained, because such freedom must
prove itself in complete openness to the encounters of life.
When man withdraws himself utterly from these encounters,
he is betraying a secret fear of them and there is no fear in
freedom.
If we wish to retain a complete openness towards the
encounters of life, we shall of course also be ready for the
pains and sorrows which are inseparable from all true
sacrifice. But we shall be without fear, for we shall realize
that pain and sorrow constantly lead us into the solitariness
of confrontation by God where the miracle of genuine
encounter with God occurs, where the certitude of the Easter
faith rises triumphant; out of the darkness of death we pass
into the light of life. And so in the midst of all pain a secret
joy is characteristic of the Christian spirit.
